predecessors.name: Duchy of Francia
predecessors.text: Hugh Capet's own lands: 'Between Paris and Orléans he possessed towns and estates amounting to approximately 400 square miles (1,000 km2)'

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: 'by the sixteenth century the "royal domain" began to coincide with the entire kingdom'

ledger.x: 987: Hugh Capet is crowned king and the royal domain begins as his own lands between Paris and Orléans.
1055: the County of Sens is annexed to the domain.
1068: Gâtinais and Château-Landon pass from Fulk IV of Anjou to the king.
1077: the French Vexin is annexed.
1101: the Viscounty of Bourges (with Dun-sur-Auron) is bought from Odo Arpin, the first foothold in Berry.
July 1185: Philip II adds the County of Amiens by the Treaty of Boves.
1191: the crown takes Péronne and its dependencies.
1200: the Norman Vexin, Évreux and Issoudun are annexed.
May 1200: by the Treaty of Le Goulet John gives up Berry.
1204: Philip II confiscates Normandy, Touraine, Anjou and Saintonge from King John.
1213: Eleanor of Vermandois dies and the rest of the county reaches the crown.
1223: Poitou is confiscated from the English.
1223: Artois, held by Prince Louis since 1191, is integrated into the domain.
1229: Raymond VII cedes lower Languedoc at the end of the Albigensian Crusade.
1237: Artois becomes an appanage of Robert I.
1241: Poitou becomes an appanage of Alphonse.
1246: Anjou becomes an apanage for Charles I of Anjou.
1271: Toulouse, Poitou and Auvergne revert to the crown on the death of Alphonse.
1284: Champagne is reunited to the domain by Philip IV's marriage to Joan I of Navarre.
1284: Chartres is bought.
1308: Angoulême, Fougères and Lusignan are bought from Yolande of Lusignan.
1308: the crown seizes La Marche on the death of the childless Count Guy.
1314: La Marche becomes an appanage of the king's youngest son.
1328: Anjou and Maine are reunited with the domain.
1336: Ponthieu is conquered (given to England in 1360).
1349: the Dauphiné is sold to the crown by the Dauphin of Viennois (1343-1349).
1349: Montpellier is bought from James III of Majorca.
1360: Berry and Auvergne go to John, Duke of Berry, as an appanage.
October 1360: the Treaty of Brétigny, ratified at Calais, cedes Poitou, Angoumois and Ponthieu with the rest of Aquitaine to Edward III.
25 October 1360: Anjou is raised to a duchy for Louis I.
1361: the king claims the Duchy of Burgundy as heir.
1364: Burgundy goes to Philip the Bold as an appanage.
1369: Charles V reopens the war and Aquitaine rises.
April 1369: Charles V reconquers Ponthieu.
1371: the crown buys the County of Auxerre.
1380: Charles V dies with the English holding 'only Calais and a few other ports'.
1392: the Orléans appanage goes to Louis I, Duke of Orléans.
1416: Berry returns to the crown on John of Berry's death and Poitou is merged into the domain.
1417: Henry V takes Caen and conquers Normandy.
January 1419: Rouen falls to Henry V and the Normandy contest ends in English hands.
19 January 1419: Rouen falls and Normandy passes to Henry V.
21 May 1420: the Treaty of Troyes makes Henry V heir and regent and Paris leaves the French crown's hands.
1422: after Charles VI's death the Dauphin rules the lands that rejected Troyes from Bourges.
20/21 September 1435: the Treaty of Arras gives Ponthieu and the Somme towns to Burgundy.
1436: with Paris recovered after the Treaty of Arras the court's seat is Paris again.
1436: the French recover Paris.
1450: Normandy is French again after Formigny.
19 October 1453: Bordeaux falls and the Hundred Years' War ends.
1477: Ponthieu is reattached.
1478: Boulogne is acquired by exchange.
10 July 1480: René dies and Louis XI adds Anjou to the domain.
1481: Charles IV, Count of Maine, dies and bequeaths his lands to Louis XI.
December 1481: Provence passes to Louis XI.
December 1482: the Treaty of Arras reattaches Burgundy and Picardy.
1498: Orléans returns to the domain at the new king's coronation.
1498: the County of Blois enters the domain.
1527: Francis I seizes La Marche.
1531: the Bourbon lands are confiscated.
1531: Angoumois returns to the royal domain.
1532: Brittany is united to France.
1558: Calais is taken back from England.
1620: Navarre and Béarn are incorporated into the crown.
1620: the royal domain is the kingdom.

wars.name: Conquest of the Angevin lands by Philip II
wars.outcome: Philip II takes Normandy and the Angevin lands from John by the end of 1204; the Battle of Bouvines (1214) 'marked the end of the Angevin Empire'.

wars.name: Albigensian Crusade
wars.outcome: The king annexed the County of Toulouse in the crusade; the 1229 Treaty of Paris cedes the two Languedoc sénéchaussées to the crown.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Brétigny (1360) cedes a third of the kingdom; Charles V reconquers most of it by 1378-1380; Troyes (1420) gives the north to Henry V; Arras (1435), Formigny (1450) and Castillon (1453) end it; Calais stays English to 1558.

certainty.note: Scattered castellanies and counties with no boundary record; the radii are my drawing.
The 1259 Treaty of Paris fixed the Aquitaine frontier, Brétigny (1360) and Arras (1435, 1482) fixed others; the imperial frontier in the east stays soft.
